newsitem.title: USA: US uncovers over 500 scams on World Wide Web.
newsitem.headline: US uncovers over 500 scams on World Wide Web.

text.p: Federal, state and local law enforcement agencies said Thursday they have found over 500 sites on the world wide web that may be promoting illegal pyramid schemes.
The agencies conducted a sweep of the Internet on Dec. 9, dubbed "Internet Pyramid Surf Day," to find sites that lure consumers with false promises of big profits from a small initial investment.
"We're putting scam artists on notice," Jodie Bernstein, director of the Federal Trade Commission's Bureau of Consumer protection, said.
"The Internet is not going to be a new marketplace where scam artists roam free," Bernstein said.

The sites were sent warnings describing characteristics of illegal pyramid schemes by electronic mail. The sites will be revisited and if evidence suggested they were illegal operations, further action would be taken, the agencies said.

In addition to the FTC, bodies that participated were the Securities and Exchange Commission, Federal Communications Commission, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, 20 state attorneys general, five state securities regulators and four district attorneys.
Some sites promoted for-profit chain letters, a common scheme outside of cyberspace as well.

"Promoting chain letters on the Internet is simply putting old wine in new bottles," Chief Postal Inspector Kenneth Hunter said. "Even though communicated via the latest telecommunications medium, electronic chain letters are identical to old fashioned scams in that they are likely to profit only the originator."
The agencies also announced a consumer education campaign backed by leading Internet service providers including AT&T Corp and America Online Inc.
Federal Trade Commission said it put educational materials on its Web site at http://www.ftc.gov/pyramid.
The Better Business Bureau said it is also distributing materials on its Web site, http://www.bbb.org, to advise consumers how to identify pyramid schemes and other online scams.
